newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open down, foreign shares suffer.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open down, foreign shares suffer.

text.p: Singapore shares opened down on Thursday, led by the foreign tranches of blue chips.
Dealers said news that Malaysia's Public Bank was proposing to alter its rules to allow overseas investors to buy its local shares caused some worries among some institutions.
"One of the concerns is that if it can happen there, it can happen here," said one dealer with a major local bank.
Foreign tranches of stocks tend to hold a premium to local tranches because they can be bought by anyone. If the rules change, this premium should disappear, dealers said.
By 0220 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials share Index (STII) was 5.14 points lower at 2,059.22. Total market volume was a low 23.1 million shares with 57 rises and 84 falls.
Most of the top losers were foreign blue chips shares.
Singapore Press foreign led the pack, falling 60 cents to Singapore $28.90. The foreign share tranches of all four big local banks lost between 20 and 40 cents each.
Public Bank foreign was down one cent at S$2.31 on 6.1 million shares after dropping to a fresh 1997 low of S$2.18.
